text:
- **chief complaint:** shortness of breath and light-headedness after playing tennis in hot, humid weather; follow-up after emergency room visit.
- **history of present illness:** the patient developed severe shortness of breath about 30 minutes into tennis, fearing a heart attack, and was taken to the ER where workup was unremarkable. About six hours later, they felt light-headed and dizzy, resolving by the next day. They report adherence to heart failure medications and reduced salt intake, though they admit occasional dietary indiscretion. Prior cataract surgery (three months ago) and skin cancer excision (five months ago) have healed without problems.
- **physical examination:** blood pressure elevated; neck supple without jugular venous distention; regular rate and rhythm, no murmur; bilateral fine lung crackles; trace bilateral lower extremity edema. ECG stable with left ventricular hypertrophy; echocardiogram shows mildly reduced but stable pumping function; skin biopsy pathology clear.
- **symptoms experienced by the patient:** shortness of breath, light-headedness, dizziness, anxiety.
- **new medications prescribed or changed:** furosemide (Lasix) 80 mg once daily as an extra dose; carvedilol 25 mg twice daily.
- **follow-up instructions:** nurse to see the patient shortly; no changes to cataract or skin cancer medications needed.
